comment: SPR-I.3.2 golden cases for chord recognition. notes are MIDI numbers as a player would hold them, lowest first. name is what the app must call them. exact is false when the reading leaves a note of the chord out, which is when alternatives are offered. These are musical judgements, not whatever the code happens to do: change one only with a reason.

cases.name: C
cases.why: a plain major triad has no symbol, as on a chart

cases.name: Csus2
cases.why: the same notes as Gsus4; the bass decides

cases.name: Gsus4
cases.why: and here the bass is G

cases.name: Cm11
cases.why: C Eb F G Bb is an m11 with the ninth left out, which is how it is played

cases.name: G7#9
cases.why: G B D F Bb: the Bb over a major third is the sharp ninth, not a minor third

cases.name: C/E
cases.why: the bass is not the root, so it is a slash chord, not a different chord

cases.name: F6
cases.why: the same notes as Dm7, and with F in the bass F6 is the reading

cases.name: Dm/F
cases.why: F D A is a D minor triad with F underneath, and nothing is missing from it

cases.name: Dm7
cases.why: and the same notes with D in the bass are Dm7

cases.name: Cadd9/D
cases.why: C major over a D: every note is named, and the D is both the ninth and the bass

cases.name: Bm7b5
cases.why: B F A has no fifth, so it is a best guess, and the same three notes are a D minor sixth without its D

cases.name: Em7
cases.why: E G B D is a chord in its own right, not a rootless Cmaj9
a third and a seventh with no root: the jazz shell, and a tritone really is two dominants, spelled the way the player asked
spelled with flats here, because the player asked for flats
